campbell.title: Campbell City Council — September 15, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered several routine city business items, including updates to the theater use policy, a cost-share agreement with the City of San Jose for resurfacing work, and the city's annual investment policy. The council also considered a budget adjustment related to replacing remaining equipment, though details on that item were cut off in the agenda.
keyTopics: Proposed modifications to Council Policy Section 14 (Theater Use Policy), effective September 16
Cost-share agreement with the City of San Jose, not to exceed $335,000, for resurfacing work
Annual update to the city's investment policy for fiscal year 2026-27
Budget adjustment to fund replacement of remaining equipment

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — September 16, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council took up routine business including meeting minutes, check registers, and a conflict of interest code update, plus final map approvals for two residential lot splits. The Council also considered two appeals of Planning Commission decisions on residential projects, and discussed options for law enforcement services ahead of upcoming town hall meetings.
keyTopics: Final map approvals for lot splits at 20517 Carniel Avenue and 19351 Saratoga Los Gatos Road
Appeal of a single-family residence and ADU design review/setback variance approval at 14650 6th Street
Appeal of a three-lot subdivision approval (Tentative Map, Design Review, CEQA exemption) at 14486 Oak Place
Discussion of law enforcement service options ahead of September 19 and 30 town hall meetings
Resolution amending the City's Conflict of Interest Code

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — September 22, 2026
los-altos.summary: The Los Altos City Council reviewed a routine set of items including a shared wastewater plant agreement, a legal services contract update, and appointments to city commissions and the VTA Board. The Council also considered an urgency ordinance placing a temporary moratorium on new detention or custodial facility applications in the city.
keyTopics: Addendum No. 14 to the Regional Water Quality Control Plant agreement with Palo Alto and Mountain View
Councilmember Weinberg's reappointment to the VTA Board
Interim urgency ordinance establishing a temporary moratorium on detention or custodial facility applications
Appointments to the Complete Streets, Environmental, and Planning Commissions
Amendment to the legal services agreement with Berliner Cohen, LLP setting a $21,500 monthly retainer

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — September 15, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council reviewed routine business, including approval of minutes from prior meetings and the town's monthly financial and investment report for July 2026. The Council also considered several contract-related items, including amendments to service agreements and new professional services agreements, along with an amendment related to heating, ventilation, and air conditioning work.
keyTopics: Monthly Financial and Investment Report for July 2026
Second Amendment to an existing agreement (authorization for the Town Manager to execute)
First Amendment to a Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning agreement
New Professional Services Agreements (Town Manager authorization)

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — September 23, 2026
san-jose.summary: The Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole reviewed the upcoming final agenda for September 29, 2026 and draft agenda for October 6, 2026, including whether to add items or set specific discussion times. The committee also considered the public record log, mayoral travel requests, and a District 1 funding request for a statewide local government association.
keyTopics: Review and finalization of the September 29, 2026 City Council agenda
Review of the draft October 6, 2026 City Council agenda
Public record review for September 10-17, 2026
Mayor's requests to travel
District 1 San Jose Sharks Community Funds allocation for the California Association of Local Agency Formation Commissions

mountain-view.title: Mountain View City Council — September 22, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The Mountain View City Council held a closed session to discuss potential legal action related to fire truck manufacturers and to consider the appointment of a City Attorney. In the regular session, the Council took up items including field renovations at Shoreline Park, a solar and battery storage energy project, updates to the Historic Preservation Ordinance and zoning map, adoption of an Active Transportation Plan, and compensation increases for the City Clerk and City Manager.
keyTopics: Closed session on potential legal action involving fire apparatus manufacturers (Golden State Fire Apparatus, Pierce, Oshkosh, REV Group, Rosenbauer, and FAMA)
Closed session consideration of a City Attorney appointment
Professional services agreement for Shoreline Athletic Fields renovation project
Various actions related to 2000 North Shoreline Boulevard
Energy services contract for solar photovoltaic systems and battery energy storage
Historic Preservation Ordinance and zoning map update
Active Transportation Plan adoption
Annual compensation increases for the City Clerk and City Manager

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — September 19, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: This was a brief special session of the Sunnyvale City Council held to present the annual State of the City address. The meeting was largely procedural, covering the event schedule before adjourning.
keyTopics: State of the City address (special meeting)
Event schedule for the session

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — September 15, 2026
cupertino.summary: The Cupertino City Council met to discuss a potential land deal with the Cupertino Union School District for property on Finch Avenue, along with anticipated litigation in closed session. In open session, the Council handled routine business including audit committee rules, a new AI usage policy, a response to a county grand jury report on pothole damage claims, and appointed two councilmembers to help select the city's next lobbyist.
keyTopics: Closed-session discussion of a potential real estate deal with Cupertino Union School District for 10480 Finch Avenue, and anticipated litigation
Introduction of an ordinance updating building code definitions for 'attic,' 'garages,' and 'square footage' (postponed to October 6, 2026)
Adoption of a new Artificial Intelligence policy for City Council use
Approval of the city's response to a Santa Clara County Civil Grand Jury report on improving pothole damage claims processes
Appointment of Mayor Kitty Moore and Councilmember Ray Wang to a subcommittee evaluating proposals for the city's 2027-2028 lobbyist

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — September 22, 2026
santa-clara.summary: The Santa Clara City Council and Stadium Authority Board held a joint meeting that opened with a closed session covering ongoing legal matters, including a case involving Silicon Valley Power against the state Department of Water Resources and a property damage claim from Travelers Insurance. The open session included several proclamations recognizing community observances and votes on HVAC control system work and office furniture purchases for city facilities.
keyTopics: Closed-session litigation update: Silicon Valley Power/Northern California Power Agency case against the California Department of Water Resources
Closed-session discussion of a property damage claim filed by Travelers Insurance on behalf of Moriel Real Estate, LLC
Deferral of an ordinance to establish new zoning rules (Chapter 18.68) for replacement housing units required under state law
Proclamations for Hispanic Heritage Month, Childhood Cancer Awareness Month, and Public Power Week
Approval items for HVAC control systems (Syserco, Inc.) and additional office furnishings (D & D Learning Spaces) for city facilities

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — September 15, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council reviewed a draft plan for how the city will use federal Community Development Block Grant funds, along with a report on the condition of the Milpitas Community Center. The Council also considered financial actions tied to winding down the former Redevelopment Agency, including issuing refunding bonds, and heard a presentation on the city's red light camera traffic safety program.
keyTopics: Draft Program Year 2025 Community Development Block Grant Consolidated Plan
Presentation on the Red Light Camera Traffic Safety Program
Presentation on the condition of the Milpitas Community Center
Resolutions related to the Successor Agency to the Redevelopment Agency, including sale and issuance of refunding bonds

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Architectural Review Board — September 17, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Architectural Review Board considered a proposed sign program for the office property at 950 Page Mill Road, which would install a shared monument sign featuring the property's own branding, 'Page Mill Labs,' along with four separate panels identifying individual tenants. The board was asked to make a recommendation on the design as part of a formal public hearing process.
keyTopics: Proposed multi-tenant monument sign at 950 Page Mill Road
Inclusion of non-tenant property branding ('Page Mill Labs') on the sign
Four tenant identification panels as part of the sign program
Determination that the project is exempt from CEQA under the accessory structures exemption
